courses.description: No description.

courses.title: Supervised Experience in College Teaching
courses.description: Provides an opportunity for supervised and graded teaching experience in undergraduate nursing courses.

courses.title: Thesis Research Off Campus
courses.description: No description.

courses.title: Ph.D. Dissertation Part-Time
courses.description: No description.

courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment of Adult Populations
courses.description: Advanced nursing assessment and diagnosis of physical, psychosocial and developmental health for adults and families across the adult age spectrum.

courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment of Pediatric Populations
courses.description: Advanced nursing assessment and diagnosis of physical, psychosocial and development health for individuals and families across the pediatric age spectrum.

courses.title: Physical Assessment Through The Lifespan
courses.description: Nursing assessment and diagnosis of physical, psychosocial, and developmental health across the lifespan. NURS 802 Physical Assessment Through The Lifespan (3) This course focuses on the comprehensive assessment of patients across the lifespan; including newborns, infants, children, pre-adolescents, adolescents, childbearing women, adults, and older adults. Comprehensive assessment includes normal changes and common health problems across the lifespan, and atypical presentations of diseases commonly seen in patient populations. Assessment instruments specific to each population group will be reviewed.

courses.title: Psych MHNP Integrative Biopsychosocial Assessment & Differential Diagnosis Across the Lifespan
courses.description: This is a comprehensive professional practice course in which students learn the Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) role focused on the biopsychosocial assessment integrating aspects of biological, familial, community, and social health. Identification and management of psychiatric diagnoses of diverse populations across the lifespan. The student will integrate newly acquired and previously mastered knowledge while developing differential diagnoses. Content focuses on epidemiological, cultural, ethical, and economic factors related to the psychiatric population in the context of diagnoses, treatment options, and quality improvement processes.

courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment Across the Lifespan Review and Competency Intensive
courses.description: This refresher course is designed for nurse practitioner students who have previously completed graduate-level advanced health assessment coursework and are returning to continue NP studies. The course provides structured review and practice of advanced physical assessment skills, diagnostic reasoning, and communication techniques across the lifespan. Students engage in selected online review activities and attend a mandatory two-day onsite intensive at Penn State Hershey to demonstrate competency through simulation, peer practice, and faculty-evaluated assessments. The course is graded Pass/Fail and ensures readiness for NP-level clinical practice.

courses.title: Pathophysiology for the Advanced Practice Nurse
courses.description: Integration of advanced physiology, developmental biology, and pathophysiology as related to specific disease entities and alterations in functioning.

courses.title: Pharmacologic Therapy for the Advanced Practice Nurse
courses.description: Pharmacologic therapies in advanced nursing practice.

courses.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course will focus on the theory and practice of cognitive behavioral therapy. The role of cognitive behavioral concepts in the care and treatment of patients will be reviewed. The care of patients with various diagnoses across different age groups will be explored.

courses.title: Population Health Perspectives
courses.description: This course explores population health concepts, measurement, and application in practice, research, and policy. This course explores population health as a framework for improving health in society. Multiple determinants will be examined in relation to health status measurement, health and disease trends, and health disparities at a community, national, and global perspective. Students will explore models for health improvement and how evidence is utilized in determining population-based intervention and policies directed at health promotion and disease prevention.

courses.title: Crisis and Trauma-Informed Care for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course will focus on crisis intervention and trauma informed care. The impact of trauma on various populations will be explored. The impact of trauma on neural, cognitive, and behavioral development will be reviewed. Students will learn about and practice current treatment approaches and interventions.

courses.title: Theoretical Foundations and Application of Psychotherapy and Advanced Therapeutic Interventions
courses.description: This integrated course focuses on the theory and application of psychotherapy and advanced therapeutic interventions in nursing practice. Through a comprehensive review of various diagnoses and the application of current treatment approaches, this course equips nursing professionals with the necessary knowledge and skills to provide holistic effective care to individuals, families and group across the lifespan.

courses.title: Family and Organizational Systems Across the Lifespan for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course introduces Bowen's family systems theory. The key theoretical concepts will be explored, and students will critically evaluate the self in relation to the family of origin. Students will also utilize critical thinking and self-reflection to apply and integrate these principles to the therapeutic relationship, as well as the care and treatment of individuals and families across the lifespan with a range of different mental health and illness states.

courses.title: Pharmacology, Pathology and Physical Assessment for Nurse Leaders
courses.description: This course is to explore the pharmacology, pathology and physical assessment processes for nurse leaders. Students will learn pharmacologic management of common diseases that occur in the major body systems, key physiologic concepts of homeostasis, regulatory mechanisms, protein function and cellular physiology. Students will consider the impact of disease processes and treatments as the apply to the spectrum of healthcare in patients and populations

courses.title: Interventions for Common Health Problems in the Adult/Older Adult
courses.description: Discussion of common health problems experienced by adults/older adults and development of evidence-based interventions for management.

courses.title: Primary Palliative Care: An Interdisciplinary Approach
courses.description: This course examines the delivery of primary palliative care from an interdisciplinary perspective. This course examines the delivery of primary palliative care in diverse populations across health care settings. Students will explore the roles of interdisciplinary healthcare professionals in the delivery of care for individuals with advanced serious illness and their family members. A holistic, person-centered approach addressing the physical, psychosocial, cultural, and spiritual delivery of primary palliative care will be examined across the life span.

courses.title: Primary Palliative Care: Interdisciplinary Management of Advanced Serious Illness
courses.description: This course examines the interdisciplinary management of persons with advanced serious illness and their family members. This course examines the interdisciplinary management of persons with advanced serious illness and their family members. Evidence-based approaches for managing the physical, psychosocial, cultural, and spiritual aspects of person-centered primary palliative care will be discussed. The course will focus on the delivery of high-quality, culturally sensitive, primary palliative care across the life-span with diverse populations in various health care settings. Holistic approaches to management from an interdisciplinary team perspective will be examined

courses.title: Interdisciplinary Practicum of the Primary Palliative Care Role
courses.description: Interdisciplinary practicum in the synthesis and application of the primary palliative care role. This course involves the practical application of knowledge acquired in previously completed courses related to primary palliative care. Students will have precepted experiences, observations, and simulated experiences to demonstrate multiple aspects of the delivery of primary palliative care. The practicum will be interdisciplinary and include various types of health care settings. The practicum will build upon and extend students' previous experiences with palliative care and fulfill mutually agreed-upon objectives based on the students' previous experiences and identified learning needs.

courses.title: Person-Centered Care: Emerging Interdisciplinary Approaches for Older Adults
courses.description: This course examines the delivery of person-centered care for older adults and their families across the health care continuum. Application of relevant theories will provide a framework of understanding and delivering care which addresses the individual's goals and behavioral episodes in the context of personal interactions and environmental factors. The importance of assessment and care planning in relation to individuals' context, personal history, and preferences for everyday living will be emphasized, while integrating care related to complex medical problems in older adults. Students will explore interdisciplinary roles, examine case studies, and identify specific interventions. The course will use a holistic approach which addresses the biological, mental/emotional, social/cultural, and spiritual delivery of person centered care to older adults and their families.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Practice I: Inquiry and Research Methods
courses.description: Foundations in evidence-based research and inquiry for nursing practice This course will provide students with the skills to incorporate evidence-based research and inquiry into nursing practice.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Practice II: Inquiry, Methods and Translation into Practice
courses.description: Principles of evidence-based practice, inquiry and skill-development to incorporate evidence-based research into nursing practice. This course emphasizes the evaluation and translation of research findings into real-world clinical applications. Through identifying and analyzing clinical phenomena that require evaluation and change, students will conduct systematic literature searches to inform their practice. This integrated approach equips nursing professionals to bridge the gap between research and practice, enhancing patient care outcomes. This course includes 75 hours of required doctoral practicum hours.

courses.title: Doctor of Nursing Practice: Leadership I
courses.description: Foundations of Doctor of Nursing Practice transformational leadership in complex health care settings.

courses.title: Doctor of Nursing Practice: Leadership II
courses.description: Doctor of Nursing Practice transformational leadership to improve healthcare delivery and quality outcomes.

courses.title: Doctor of Nursing Practice Clinical Practicum
courses.description: The focus of the clinical practicum is planning, implementing, and evaluating evidence-based interventions to address a healthcare problem.

courses.title: Nurse Practitioner Doctoral Practicum
courses.description: This Nurse Practitioner Doctoral Practicum allows the student to integrate the role of the DNP-prepared, option-specific NP, demonstrating clinical competency, diagnostic reasoning, and clinical decision-making abilities while contributing to a culture of clinical scholarship among all healthcare professionals. Clinical experiences are conducted with guidance from NP option-specific clinical preceptors and clinical faculty. The settings for student rotations in the clinical practicum course are appropriate to the option-specific NP role and may be chosen based upon a student's preferred specialty area.

courses.title: Doctor of Nursing Practice Project
courses.description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice capstone project demonstrates clinical scholarship in an area of practice.

courses.title: Healthcare Informatics
courses.description: This course provides a foundation in information systems and technology for improvement of healthcare.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Practice III: Project Development
courses.description: The Doctor of Nursing Practice (D.N.P.) project plan will be developed focusing on design, sample, data collection, projected outcomes, resourcing, plan for analysis, and sustainability. Students will collaborate with key stakeholders to build project support. Students will complete steps for Institutional Review Board (IRB) submission. The course includes 75 hours of required clinical practicum hours.

courses.title: Nursing Education Theories and Strategies
courses.description: Theoretical foundation and evidence-based strategies for nursing education. NURS 840 Nursing Education Theories and Strategies (3) This course provides a foundation in the role of the nurse educator and evidence-based strategies for nursing education. Students will explore various theoretical perspectives of teaching and learning, as well as practical application of strategies to meet the diverse needs of learners. The course is intended to prepare students to employ effective teaching strategies in classroom, clinical, and on-line educational settings. Discussion of managing various challenges related to nursing education will be included throughout the course.

courses.title: Assessment and Evaluation in Nursing Education
courses.description: Methods for assessment, measurement, and evaluation of student learning in academic and clinical settings. NURS 841 Assessment and Evaluation in Nursing Education (3) This course provides a foundation in assessment, measurement, and evaluation strategies for nursing education. Students will explore the theoretical basis for evaluation, as well as practical application of the strategies. The course is intended to prepare students to utilize strategies of measurement and evaluation in developing tests, interpreting test results, assessing clinical performance, and evaluating written assignments. Discussion of legal and ethical issues related to evaluation in nursing education will be included throughout the course.

courses.title: Curriculum and Program Development in Nursing Education
courses.description: Curriculum design and evaluation, educational program development, and accreditation. NURS 842 Curriculum and Program Development in Nursing Education (3) This course provides a foundation in curricular design, program development, and curriculum evaluation in nursing education. Students will explore internal and external contextual factors influencing curriculum design and implementation. This course is intended to prepare students to utilize foundational principles and concepts for the development and evaluation of nursing curricula in academic settings. This course will also prepare students for program development and evaluation in nursing education.

courses.title: Synthesis and Application of the Nurse Educator Role
courses.description: This capstone practicum course involves the practical application of knowledge from previously completed courses related to the nurse educator role and advanced nursing care delivery in academic and healthcare settings. Students will work with a preceptor in an educational/healthcare settings to demonstrate multiple aspects of the nurse educator role. In addition, students will demonstrate a direct care role through clinical experiences designed to strengthen patient care delivery skills. The practicum experiences will be developed to fulfill mutually agreed-upon objectives based on students' previous experiences and identified learning needs.

courses.title: Healthcare Economics and Policy for Nurse Administrators
courses.description: Concepts of healthcare economics and policy for nurse administrators

courses.title: Leadership Concepts and Theories for Nurse Administrators
courses.description: Concepts and theories of leadership for nurse administrators. NURS 846 Leadership Concepts and Theories for Nurse Administrators (3) This course provides a foundation in nurse leadership roles, concepts, and theories. Students will explore the theoretical basis of leadership and change, as well as analyze organizational structure, power, and politics. This course is intended to provide students with a theoretical and evidence-based foundation for leadership roles within health care organizations. Discussion of communication, decision-making, and problem-solving strategies for nurse administrators is included throughout the course.

courses.title: Human Resource and Work Force Issues for Nurse Administrators
courses.description: Human resource management and work force issues for nurse administrators. NURS 847 Human Resource and Work Force Issues for Nurse Administrators (3) This course provides a foundation in human resources within health care organizations. Students will examine ethical and legal issues related to collective bargaining, unions, and staffing. This course is intended to prepare students to utilize leadership strategies for recruiting, retaining, developing, and evaluating a diverse, multidisciplinary work force in complex healthcare environments. Discussion of evidence-based strategies for conflict resolution will be included throughout the course.

courses.title: Synthesis and Application of the Nurse Administrator Role
courses.description: This course involves the practical application of knowledge acquired in previously completed courses related to nurse administration. Students will work with a preceptor in a health care setting to demonstrate multiple aspects of the nurse administrator role. The practicum experience will be developed to fulfill mutually agreed-upon objectives based on students' previous experiences and identified learning needs.

courses.title: Synthesis and Application of the Nurse Administrator Role
courses.description: This course involves the practical application of knowledge acquired in previously completed courses related to the nurse administrator. Students will work with a preceptor in a health care setting to demonstrate multiple aspects of the nurse administrator role. The practicum experience will be developed to fulfill mutually agreed-upon objectives based on students' previous experiences and identified learning needs. This course is specifically designed as a practicum course for students in the B.S.N. to D.N.P. program and evaluated based on the nationally acknowledged foundational competencies that are core to all advanced nursing practice roles and known as the D.N.P. Essentials (AACN, 2006).

courses.title: General Linear Modeling in Health Research: Foundations, Approaches, and Applications A
courses.description: In this course students will learn the foundations of general and generalized linear models in health science research. The course will introduce students to generalized linear modeling covering core concepts, assumptions, and examples from nursing research and related health sciences. Students will learn the skills to explore and evaluate common health data sources such as electronic medical records, vital statistics registries, primary and secondary data sets (e.g. clinical trials, Health and Retirement Study) for use in generalized linear modeling analyses. Students will also develop the skills to evaluate generalized linear modeling results within their chosen nursing areas and effectively communicate their analysis findings.

courses.title: General Linear Modeling in Health Research: Foundations, Approaches, and Applications B
courses.description: In this course students will build on the knowledge and skills learned in NURS851A and move to the applications of general and generalized linear models in health science research. Students will learn the process of developing and testing hypotheses including hypotheses testing mediation and moderation. Students will also identify the quantitative and clinical assumptions of models, apply model-building techniques, and calculate the appropriate effect sizes. Using common statistical analysis software packages, students will develop the skills needed for interdisciplinary collaborations on health science research projects using these models.

courses.title: Chemistry and Physics for Nurse Anesthesia
courses.description: This doctoral-level course provides a rigorous foundation in chemistry, biochemistry, and physics with direct application to nurse anesthesia practice. Through problem-based learning, case analysis, and integration of simulation exercises, students will apply these scientific concepts to real-world clinical scenarios, emphasizing anesthesia patient safety. The course supports competency development in clinical judgment, systems-based safety, and evidence-based decision-making.

courses.title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description: This doctoral-level course delivers an advanced, in-depth exploration of human anatomy and physiology across the lifespan. Structure-function relationships are covered from a molecular, cellular, tissue, organ, and system perspective. Topics include physiologic differences related to culture, gender, race, age, and genetics. Learners will develop the capacity to synthesize advanced biophysical knowledge into real-time decision-making, laying the scientific foundation for advanced pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical practice, and patient management. Various techniques will be used to reinforce systems thinking and support application in diverse patient populations.

courses.title: Principles of Nurse Anesthesia Practice I: Basic Principles
courses.description: This doctoral-level course is the first in a series of four courses that includes core principles and competencies required for safe and effective nurse anesthesia practice across the lifespan. Students develop essential clinical skills in anesthesia-specific patient assessment and evaluation, operating room preparation, perioperative monitoring and data interpretation, diagnostic reasoning, and preoperative documentation. Content includes basic airway assessment and management, the anesthesia machine, anesthesia equipment, and anesthetic monitoring systems. Simulation-based learning (12 hours) is integrated to enhance psychomotor skills related to the preparation of the operating environment and patient preparation. The course emphasizes professional vigilance, critical thinking, and situational awareness.

courses.title: Advanced Pathophysiology Across the Lifespan
courses.description: This advanced doctoral-level course builds upon advanced physiologic principles by focusing on pathophysiologic considerations of populations across the lifespan. The course will focus on the relationship of pathophysiology to clinical assessment, decision-making, and management. Evidence-based treatment and clinical management for disease states and conditions will be discussed. Through case-based learning and evidence-informed discussions, students demonstrate the ability to integrate biophysical science with individualized, safe clinical care.

courses.title: Advanced Pharmacology for Anesthesia Practice
courses.description: This doctoral-level course prepares students for the safe and effective pharmacologic management of patients across the lifespan in the perioperative setting. Students explore the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of various anesthetic agents, with particular attention to how patient-specific variables - including age, comorbidities, and organ function - affect drug selection, metabolism, and patient response. Through the integration of evidence-based guidelines, learners analyze clinical scenarios and apply pharmacologic reasoning to individualized anesthetic patient management. Students will formulate risk mitigation strategies to prevent drug errors, adverse events, and medication interactions.

courses.title: Principles of Nurse Anesthesia Practice II: Advanced Principles
courses.description: This doctoral-level course is the second in a series of four courses that includes core principles and competencies required for safe and effective nurse anesthesia practice across the lifespan. This course prepares students for entry into clinical practice by discussing concepts such as patient positioning, anesthetic administration, and the induction of, maintenance of, and emergence from anesthesia. Emphasis will be placed on formulation and evaluation of anesthetic plans, communication and documentation, and anesthetic techniques and complications. Simulation scenarios integrate patient monitoring, induction of general anesthesia, procedural skills, and team-based communication. A structured operating room (OR) shadowing experience bridges academic preparation with the expectations of immersive clinical practice. This course ensures students demonstrate readiness to enter the clinical environment with competence, confidence, and an ethical, safety-driven mindset.

courses.title: Principles of Nurse Anesthesia Practice III: Special Procedures and Populations I
courses.description: This doctoral-level course is the third in a series of four courses that includes core principles and competencies required for safe and effective nurse anesthesia practice across the lifespan. This course prepares students to manage complex anesthesia scenarios by integrating advanced techniques, interprofessional collaboration, and clinical judgment. Students will learn evidence-based techniques for the management of patients undergoing a variety of diagnostic, therapeutic, and surgical procedures. The course emphasizes a team-based approach to anesthetic crisis management and safety through 12 hours of simulation to practice crisis management and procedural skills. The course reinforces ethical and safe decision-making, clinical adaptability, and the delivery of person-centered, high-quality anesthesia care in complex and evolving environments.

courses.title: Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Role I
courses.description: Acute Care Nurse Practitioner role across the continuum of care with adults and older adults with complex acute, critical, and chronic health conditions to restore or maximize health. This course focuses on utilization of a collaborative approach to enhance Acute Care Nurse Practitioner effectiveness with restorative care and synthesis of theoretical, scientific, and clinical knowledge required for the assessment, diagnosis, management, and treatment options of patients with complex acute, critical, and chronic illness across the continuum of care. Content will focus on patients with acute and chronic cardiovascular, pulmonary, infectious disease, and nutrition problems, as well as related ethical, legal, and professional practice issues. This course is designed to be taken concurrently with the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Practicum I ( NURS 862 ) and is required for the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Option within the Master of Science degree with a major in Nursing.

courses.title: Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Role II
courses.description: Continuation of Acute Care Nurse Practitioner role across the continuum of care with adults and older adults with complex acute, critical, and chronic health conditions to restore or maximize health. NURS 861 Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Role II (3)This course continues the focus on utilization of a collaborative approach to enhance Acute Care Nurse Practitioner effectiveness with restorative care and synthesis of theoretical, scientific, and clinical knowledge required for the assessment, diagnosis, management, and treatment options of patients with complex acute, critical, and chronic illness across the continuum of care. Content will focus on patients with acute and chronic neurologic, gastrointestinal, renal, hematologic, and endocrine problems, as well as special topics. This course is designed to be taken concurrently with the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Practicum II ( NURS 863 ) and is required for the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Option within the Master of Science degree with a major in Nursing.

courses.title: Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Practicum I
courses.description: Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner practicum with patients across the continuum of care with adults and older adults with complex acute, critical, and chronic health conditions. This is a comprehensive practicum in which students implement the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner role through application of theoretical knowledge and psychomotor skills taught in NURS 860 and all prior courses. Emphasis is given to development of clinical competency and clinical decision making abilities. This practicum course for the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner option involves student rotations through clinical sites providing care for adults and older adults with acute and critical illness. Clinical conferences will enable students to discuss their unique clinical experiences and topics that emerge from their clinical practice. Minimum clinical conference time is 15 hours per semester.

courses.title: Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner Doctoral Practicum I
courses.description: This is a comprehensive practicum in which students implement the Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner role through application of theoretical knowledge and psychomotor skills taught in NURS 860 and all prior courses. This practicum allows the student to integrate the roles of the DNP prepared Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, demonstrate clinical competency and clinical decision-making abilities, and contribute to a culture of clinical scholarship among all health care professionals. Clinical experiences are conducted with guidance from a clinical preceptor and clinical faculty oversight. courses.title: Principles of Nurse Anesthesia Practice IV: Special Procedures and Populations II
courses.description: This doctoral-level course is the final course in a series of four courses that includes core principles and competencies required for safe and effective nurse anesthesia practice across the lifespan. courses.title: Clinical Practicum I
courses.description: This is the first in a series of six clinical practicum courses. Learners will enter the clinical environment and apply peri-anesthetic concepts and didactic knowledge into clinical anesthetic practice. Emphasis is placed on orientation to the anesthetic environment, patient safety, vigilance, communication, preoperative assessment and evaluation, comprehensive equipment preparation, and prevention of complications. The creation of tailored, patient-specific anesthetic management plans is complemented by experiential learning, allowing application of skills and knowledge learned in the didactic curriculum. Clinical competency is assessed through performance in the clinical environment.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum II

Emphasis is placed on patient safety, vigilance, culturally competent care of the patient across the peri-anesthetic continuum, critical thinking, and interpersonal communication. Clinical competency is assessed through performance in the clinical environment.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum III

Clinical experiences focus on anesthesia care of complex and diverse patient populations across the lifespan undergoing elective and emergency surgical and medical procedures. Emphasis is placed on patient safety, vigilance, culturally competent care of the patient across the peri-anesthetic continuum, critical thinking, and interpersonal communication. Clinical competency is assessed through performance in the clinical environment.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum IV

courses.title: Professional Role in Nurse Anesthesia
courses.description: This doctoral-level course examines the professional role development of the Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA) within evolving and complex healthcare systems. Students explore critical domains of CRNA practice including healthcare finance, business operations, practice management models, informatics, information systems/technology, and ethical leadership. Students critically examine healthcare policy, advocacy strategies, leadership, and the role of CRNAs in shaping legislative and organizational change. Additional focus is placed on personal and professional wellness, with specific attention to burnout prevention, stress management, and substance use disorders in anesthesia providers. The course cultivates self-awareness, professional identity, and ethical decision-making, empowering students to lead with competence, compassion, and integrity in diverse anesthesia practice settings.

Students will critically analyze, synthesize, and evaluate the knowledge gained in previous nurse anesthesia coursework and clinical practicum courses through a review of evidence-based anesthesia literature. Students will be given the opportunity to develop an independent study plan with faculty guidance. Students will participate in structured review sessions, password protected exams, and mock boards to review comprehensive topics encountered on the NBCRNA Self-Evaluation Exam (SEE) and the NCE. Students will complete the SEE in compliance with program policy.
